name: District of Columbia
sources: Rate table, standard deduction, 65+/blind add-on, itemizing rules (federal itemizing required, no SALT cap, state income tax excluded), OBBBA decoupling: 2025 D-40 booklet, https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/otr/publication/attachments/2025_D40_Book_082026_v1.pdf

2026 standard deduction = 2025 amounts adjusted for cost of living, through 2029 (B26-0724 emergency act / B26-0661 permanent act): EY Tax News 2026-1962, https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1962 and https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1981-state-and-local-tax-weekly-for-august-21-and-august-28
provisional: Standard deduction uses the 2025 amounts ($15,000 single/MFS, $30,000 joint, $22,500 head of household); DC law adjusts them for cost of living for 2026, but the 2026 amounts are not yet published.
Extra deduction for 65+ uses the 2025 married amount ($1,600 per person); single and head-of-household filers actually get $2,000, and the 2026 amounts are not yet published.
Rate table is the one in force since 2022 (2025 booklet); no 2026 change was found.
notes: Itemized deductions are cut by 5% of income over $200,000 ($100,000 married filing separately); that limit is not applied here.
Married couples can often pay less by filing separately on the same return; this estimate assumes a joint return.
